I had a kitchen fire. I am documenting my repairs.

Looks pretty good.

A little question, where did you learn those repairing skills? From the internet?

I've been living in country side for most of my youth, which enabled me to have tools and materials around. I have been always been tinkering with stuff.

Whenever I need to do something a bit more advanced, I spend couple of hours researching what I am doing. Actually even reading research papers on latest techniques. Like when I built the living room wooden floor you see in the first video slides, I spent maybe 50 hours just reading up on how this type of floor is supposed to be built and how does the subfloor work. I actually had to rebuild everything up from the ground, as the subfloor wasn't in reusable condition.

I also try to utilize my other tangential skills. Like I had to 3D model the stairs multiple times to get them to fit in that very tight space so I could walk them up and down without hitting my head. And sufficient slope as not to be completely like a ladder :)

I have to admit, my jointery is appalling, but hey, I build the stuff for usage, not for looks. "Good enough, hide the crimes, etc." :P
Well I'm a city boy, but would really like to learn those skills, but internet doesn't seem to help much yet. Anyway have fun with your repaired house. :)
